title: Tiled roofs (western Turkey)
description: Orange clay-tiled roofs dominate the western half of Turkey, fading out through central-eastern Anatolia. Turkey can be regionguessed with roof types: tiled roofs in the western half, flat roofs in the south-east, metal roofs in the eastern half and pyramid roofs around Lake Van.

title: Flat roofs (south-eastern Turkey)
description: Flat-roofed concrete houses are typical of south-eastern Turkey, along the Syrian border from Gaziantep to Hakkari, thinning out towards Adana and Hatay. Turkey can be regionguessed with roof types: tiled roofs in the western half, flat roofs in the south-east, metal roofs in the eastern half and pyramid roofs around Lake Van.

title: Corrugated metal roofs (eastern Turkey)
description: Corrugated metal roofs are common in the eastern half of Turkey, especially in the north-east (Erzurum, Kars, Ağrı, Van), less so around Sivas, Malatya and Elazığ; a small pocket also exists in the Taurus south of Karaman. Turkey can be regionguessed with roof types: tiled roofs in the western half, flat roofs in the south-east, metal roofs in the eastern half and pyramid roofs around Lake Van.

title: Pyramid roofs around Lake Van
description: Square houses with pyramid-shaped (hipped) metal roofs are typical of the area around Lake Van. Turkey can be regionguessed with roof types: tiled roofs in the western half, flat roofs in the south-east, metal roofs in the eastern half and pyramid roofs around Lake Van.

title: Purple rhododendrons east of Istanbul
description: Bushes with purple flowers (rhododendron/azalea) are a strong clue for the area around İzmit, east of Istanbul. They grow across the country but only bloom in May, and May coverage is limited to this area.

title: Cedars of the southern Taurus
description: Cedars of Lebanon grow in southern Turkey, roughly between Antalya and Gaziantep, along the Taurus mountains. They are recognisable by long horizontal branches with wide foliage; in the harsher southern Turkish mountains they look more like larches while keeping their horizontal branch structure.

title: Snowflake street lamps of Kars
description: Street lamps in Kars have a triangular frame decorated with small snowflakes. They are rare even in the city and similar styles may exist in other towns, so use with caution.

title: Horizontal pole plates around Kayseri
description: Around Kayseri, electricity poles carry horizontal plates with blue lettering.

title: Yellow-doubled lane lines (south-east)
description: In south-eastern Turkey, white lane-separation lines are sometimes doubled with a yellow line.

title: Pigeon dropping on the Google car roof (west of Uşak)
description: A Google car generation in Turkey has a pigeon dropping at the top right of the roof; it is found west of Uşak, between Manisa and Uşak.

title: Bent raised antenna (west of Antalya)
description: A Google car with a raised, slightly curved antenna is found west of Antalya, roughly between Burdur, Fethiye and Kaş.

title: Rumble strips on divided highways
description: Only two major divided highways in Turkey have rumble strips on their edges, both running east-west: a northern one (Çorum–Amasya–Tokat–Erzincan) and a southern one (Mersin–Adana–Gaziantep–Şanlıurfa–Mardin–Nusaybin), the E80 and E90. The landscapes are distinct, so this effectively gives the road.
